# nuxt-telegram-auth

> Nuxt auth module for Telegram Login on Nuxt 4.6 or newer. Users log in through a popup button or the OAuth and OpenID Connect redirect. The server verifies Telegram's id_token and keeps the session in a sealed, HttpOnly cookie, with no database.

Install with `npx nuxi module add nuxt-telegram-auth`. Set `NUXT_PUBLIC_TELEGRAM_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` and a session secret `NUXT_APP_SECRET` (at least 32 characters), and turn on Telegram Login for the bot in the BotFather Mini App. New apps use `<TelegramLoginButton>` and `useTelegramSession()`. `<TelegramLoginWidget>` is the legacy widget for bots that have not switched to Telegram Login.

## Docs

- [Home](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/): overview and features
- [Quickstart](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/installation.html): install, session secret, BotFather setup and a login button
- [Telegram Login](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/telegram-login.html): Telegram OAuth with popup and redirect login, allowed URLs, errors and nuxt-security
- [Sessions and hooks](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/sessions.html): useTelegramSession(), server utilities, hooks and the session cookie
- [Page protection](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/pages.html): definePageMeta({ telegramAuth: true }) and its options
- [Configuration](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/configuration.html): environment variables, module options and routes
- [Legacy widget options](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/properties.html): props and events of the old TelegramLoginWidget component
- [Redirect mode (legacy widget)](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/redirect-mode.html): redirect mode of the old widget
- [Migrating from 1.x](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/migration.html): upgrading to 2.0 and moving to Telegram Login
- [Telegram login widget generator](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/telegram-login-widget/): pick button or legacy widget options and copy the component, nuxt.config and .env code

## Blog

- [Blog index](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/): guides to Telegram login and Nuxt authentication
- [Telegram Mini Apps and the login widget: which one signs users in](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/telegram-mini-app-vs-login-widget.html): Telegram Mini Apps sign users in with initData, websites use Telegram Login or the old widget. How each works, how to verify it, what this module covers.
- [nuxt-auth-utils or nuxt-telegram-auth: what each module does](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/nuxt-auth-utils-vs-nuxt-telegram-auth.html): nuxt-auth-utils and nuxt-telegram-auth both seal the session in a cookie. Compare providers, page protection, hooks and Telegram support before you pick one.
- [Nuxt auth in 2026: the main modules compared](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/nuxt-authentication-options.html): An overview of Nuxt auth modules: nuxt-auth-utils, sidebase nuxt-auth, the Supabase module and nuxt-telegram-auth, with what each one handles and needs.
- [Nuxt auth middleware: protecting pages and server routes](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/nuxt-auth-middleware.html): How Nuxt route middleware protects pages, why server routes need their own check, and how nuxt-telegram-auth does both with definePageMeta and one helper.
- [Sealed cookies or JWTs for Nuxt sessions](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/nuxt-sealed-cookies-vs-jwt.html): Why nuxt-telegram-auth keeps sessions in one sealed HttpOnly cookie instead of a JWT in the browser, and where a JWT still appears in the Telegram login flow.
- [Verifying a Telegram login on the server](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/telegram-login-verification.html): How a Telegram login is checked on the server: id_token, JWKS, nonce, state and PKCE for Telegram OAuth, and the HMAC hash check for the legacy login widget.
- [Saving Telegram users to a database when they log in](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/telegram-login-save-users.html): Use nuxt-telegram-auth's server hooks to save Telegram users to your database, add a role to the session or refuse a login, with what each hook receives.
- [BotFather setup for Telegram Login: Allowed URLs and client ID](https://projects.halit.org/nuxt-telegram-auth/blog/botfather-login-widget-setup.html): Step by step BotFather setup for Telegram Login: create the bot, open Login Widget, add Allowed URLs, copy the Client ID and Secret, and pick a signing key.
